title: Philippines eyes more Filipino products in South Korea amid trade talks

blocks.text: The Philippines is eyeing more opportunities for Filipino exporters to sell their products in South Korea amid ongoing discussions to upgrade the free trade agreement between the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and Seoul.

During the 27th ASEAN–Republic of Korea Summit chaired by President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. on Monday, both sides aim to achieve a substantial conclusion of their upgraded free trade pact by the end of 2027 to help expand market access across the region.

In his speech, Marcos underscored the more than three decades of relations between the regional bloc and South Korea, noting that the nations are pursuing greater opportunities for regional cooperation across various fields through the Plan of Action 2026 to 2030.

“Over three decades, our relations have evolved into a comprehensive strategic partnership grounded in mutual trust, shared interest, and a common vision for peace, stability, and prosperity. Our cooperation is now guided by the ASEAN-Republic of Korea Plan of Action 2026 to 2030,” Marcos said.

The Plan of Action outlines joint efforts to bolster maritime safety and energy security, leverage artificial intelligence for digital advancement, and deepen partnerships in healthcare as well as technical and vocational education and training.
Marcos also welcomed Seoul’s sustained backing of the bloc’s long-term goals and regional leadership.

“We welcome the Republic of Korea's continued support for ASEAN Community Vision 2045, ASEAN centrality, and ASEAN-led mechanisms. We look forward to strengthening our cooperation in upholding international law and advancing an open, inclusive, and peaceful region,” the President said. — BAP, GMA News
